items.followUp: Why is a hypothesis tested through experiments?

rubric.why: A hypothesis provides a basis or direction for investigating a biological problem.
rubric.description: Explains that a hypothesis directs the investigation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its role as the basis or direction of the investigation.

rubric.why: Experiments are planned to test the hypothesis.
rubric.description: States that experiments test the hypothesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the hypothesis to experimental testing.

modelAnswer: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation that provides a basis and direction for investigating a biological problem.
Experiments test whether the hypothesis is correct.

items.followUp: State two functions of the epidermis in plants.

rubric.why: Epidermal tissues help limit water loss from the plant.
rubric.description: States that the plant may lose excessive water or dry out.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this consequence of lacking epidermal tissue.

rubric.why: The epidermis protects the plant from injury and harmful organisms.
rubric.description: States that the plant is more vulnerable to injury or infection.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second consequence of lacking epidermal tissue.

modelAnswer: Without epidermal tissues, a plant would lose more water and may dry out.
It would also be less protected from mechanical injury and pathogens.

rubric.why: Osmosis specifically involves water moving through a selectively permeable membrane.
rubric.description: Gives the defining feature of osmosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying water movement through a selectively permeable membrane.

rubric.why: Diffusion is the net movement of particles down a concentration gradient and does not require a membrane.
rubric.description: Gives the defining feature of diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that particles move from higher to lower concentration, or that diffusion does not require a membrane.

modelAnswer: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution.
Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration; it does not require a membrane.

items.followUp: What happens to a cell when it enters the G₀ phase?

rubric.why: In G₀, the cell leaves the active cell cycle.
rubric.description: Identifies G₀ as a phase in which the cell exits the active cell cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cell leaves or exits the cell cycle.

rubric.why: A cell in G₀ does not divide, although it can continue carrying out its normal functions.
rubric.description: States that the cell does not divide or continues its normal functions while in G₀.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the cell’s state or activity in G₀.

modelAnswer: In the G₀ phase, a cell leaves the active cell cycle and does not divide.
It may remain metabolically active while carrying out its normal functions.
